structured_result.summary: Focused read-only review of the correction candidate at /private/tmp/task-runners-fixes-dcl15558. The diagnostics version parser now accepts X.Y.Z, plus -alpha.N, -beta.N and -rc.N with a numeric ordinal, and still withholds arbitrary suffixes, build metadata and extra lines. Readiness still requires a recognized version and authenticated status, and the regression tests are thorough. In xtask, --skip-build and --binary now require each other, the normal build uses Cargo's reported artifact, and the stale target_dir default is gone. One low-priority regression was found: the documented wrapper scripts/package.sh changes into the repository root before forwarding options, so a relative --binary resolves from the repository root instead of the caller's working directory, contradicting the new README contract.

findings.title: package.sh changes into the repo root, so a relative --binary resolves from the wrong directory
findings.scenario: From /work, a user runs `/repo/scripts/package.sh --host both --skip-build --binary out/task-runners`, expecting /work/out/task-runners to be packaged.
findings.evidence: scripts/package.sh:4-6 changes into the repository root and then runs `cargo xtask package "$@"`. xtask select_binary (xtask/src/main.rs:143-149) calls std::path::absolute(binary), which resolves against the process cwd, now the repo root. README.md:49 says relative binary paths resolve from the caller's current working directory, and README.md:51 says package.sh is a thin alias that forwards these options. No test covers a relative --binary passed through the script.
findings.impact: The relative path silently refers to /repo/out/task-runners instead. The result is either a confusing 'executable missing' error or, if a file exists there, packaging a different and possibly stale executable. That second case is the hazard this correction was meant to remove.
findings.suggested_correction: In package.sh, keep the caller's cwd: drop the cd and run `cargo --manifest-path "$task_runners_root/Cargo.toml" xtask package "$@"` (or call cargo run with --manifest-path), or convert a relative --binary argument to an absolute path against the original $PWD before cd. Alternatively, document that paths passed through package.sh resolve from the repository root.

findings.title: Preserve caller-relative binary paths through the packaging alias
findings.scenario: Invoke /path/to/checkout/scripts/package.sh --skip-build --binary ./task-runners from a directory containing the intended executable.
findings.evidence: The alias changes directory to the checkout before forwarding arguments. xtask/src/main.rs:149 then resolves --binary using std::path::absolute against that changed directory. README promises caller-relative paths and describes this script as an alias forwarding the options. Existing regression tests exercise select_binary directly, bypassing the script.
findings.impact: Packaging rejects an existing caller-relative executable or silently packages a different checkout-relative executable if one exists at the same relative path.
findings.suggested_correction: Preserve the original caller directory when resolving --binary through the script, or normalize the binary argument before changing directories. Add a regression covering invocation from another directory with distinct intended and checkout-relative binaries.
